<Aside type="caution" title="Superseded (2026-06-04) — verify against current code">
The premise of **Trap 1** no longer holds. The whole tooldef re-export chain
moved to ESM together on 2026-06-04: `@papercusp/tooldef`, `@papercusp/tooldef-http`,
`@papercusp/tooldef-mcp`, `@papercusp/agent-mcp`, **and** `@papercusp/chat-protocol`
all now carry `"type": "module"`. So a new sibling should now **match the family by
setting `"type": "module"`** — the opposite of the rule below. (The page's own
escape hatch — "if you genuinely need ESM, move the whole re-export chain together"
— is exactly what happened.) Note the build configs still emit CJS
(`tsconfig.build.json`: `"module": "CommonJS"`), which is now mismatched with the
package `"type"`; the runtime that matters is `tsx`, which honors `"type"`.

**Trap 2** is also weakened: the operator + operator-core now compile under
`"moduleResolution": "bundler"` (not classic `node`), so the `exports` map *is*
honored. The top-level `main`/`types` belt-and-suspenders is still present and
harmless, but the "classic node ignores exports" rationale no longer describes
these consumers. The "verify under real `tsx`/Node, not just vitest" advice at the
bottom still stands.
</Aside>

When you scaffold a **new** workspace package and wire it into the
`@papercusp/tooldef` family (src-as-entry packages — `main`/`types`/`exports`
all point at `./src/index.ts`, consumed via a direct `node_modules/@papercusp/<pkg>`
symlink), two `package.json` fields decide whether the **operator host** can load
it at runtime. Both default to the wrong thing, and both are **masked by the test
runner**, so green unit tests are not proof the host works.

## Trap 1 — `"type": "module"` in a CJS family

`@papercusp/tooldef` and `@papercusp/agent-mcp` are **CommonJS** (their
`tsconfig.build.json` emits CJS; no `type` field → Node treats `.js`/`.ts` as CJS).
The operator's `:3070` Hono host runs under **`tsx`**, which honours `type`.

If you give a new sibling (`@papercusp/tooldef-http`, `@papercusp/tooldef-mcp`,
…) `"type": "module"`, then importing a **named** binding across the CJS↔ESM
boundary throws under tsx:

```
SyntaxError: The requested module '@papercusp/tooldef' does not provide an
export named 'dispatchProjectedTool'
```

— the classic CJS↔ESM named-export interop break (the named binding isn't
statically visible across the boundary). **Observed directly:** the standalone
`examples/standalone-http.ts` proof failed with exactly this under both node 22
and node 25 while the packages carried `"type": "module"`.

**Why it hides:** `vitest`/`esbuild` transpile everything to a single module
graph and don't enforce the CJS/ESM boundary, so the package's own test suite
passes 100%. The break only appears under real Node/tsx module resolution — a
`npx tsx examples/…` script, or the operator's `:3070` Hono host, which runs
under the same tsx runtime and imports these packages (via `agent-mcp`'s
re-export) — so the host is exposed to the same break. During the extraction the
bug was invisible until the standalone example ran it under tsx.

**Verified after the fix (2026-05-31, live host):** with `"type"` removed, the
operator's `:3070` Hono host (`bin/hono-host.ts` under tsx, node 22) boots clean
on the fixed packages and serves both transports end-to-end — a live HTTP
projected-tool call returns `200` + the `{content}` envelope (`tooldef-http`),
and MCP `tools/call` dispatches projected tools through `tooldef-mcp`. (The
caveat the examples teach still stands: only `tsx`/real-Node resolution exercises
this boundary; the bundled test suite won't.)

**Rule:** a new package that any CJS package re-exports from (or that the tsx
host imports) must **not** set `"type": "module"`. Match the family — omit
`type` (CJS). If you genuinely need ESM, the whole re-export chain has to move
together, which the family deliberately hasn't done.

## Trap 2 — `"exports"` without top-level `"main"`/`"types"`

The operator + several consumers compile under **classic `moduleResolution:
node`** (not `node16`/`bundler`). Classic resolution **ignores the `exports`
map** and looks only at top-level `"main"`/`"types"`. A `package.json` like:

```jsonc
{ "exports": { ".": { "types": "./src/index.ts", "import": "./src/index.ts" } } }
```

resolves fine under `tsx`/bundler but fails a consumer's `tsc` with
`Cannot find module '@papercusp/<pkg>'`. This is exactly why
`@papercusp/chat-protocol` "didn't exist" until its submodule `package.json`
gained top-level `main`/`types`.

**Rule:** every src-as-entry package ships **both** — top-level
`"main": "./src/index.ts"` + `"types": "./src/index.ts"` **and** the `exports`
map. Belt and suspenders covers both resolver modes.

## How to actually verify (don't trust the test suite)

The package's own `vitest` is necessary but **not sufficient**. Before claiming a
new package works in the host:

1. Write a `examples/standalone-*.ts` that imports only the package(s) under test
   and run it with `npx tsx examples/<x>.ts`. This exercises real Node/tsx
   resolution and the CJS/ESM boundary the bundler hides.
2. If it's on the host's import path, reload the Tauri shell (server-side code
   has no hot-reload) and exercise the route — a green tsc + green vitest can
   still ship a host that won't boot.

See also [`generalizing-a-lib-host-seam-pattern`](/agent-insights/generalizing-a-lib-host-seam-pattern)
for the src-as-entry + symlink recipe these packages follow, and the plan
`papercusp-tooldef-extraction-2026-05-29` (P-051) for the commit that fixed it.
